title: Report unreadable directories repo-relative in the crawl

completion.statement: The crawl's os.walk onerror handler now reports unreadable directories repo-relative via os.path.relpath(error.filename, root), so a chmod-000 directory names only its repo-relative path in not_determined; no absolute, home or leading-slash path reaches the JSON report or the committed CODEBASE.md artifact. Honest degradation is preserved: the entry is named, the rest of the tree still scans, and the run exits 0 with the warning. A chmod-000 fixture regression test in tests/test_crawl.py fails before the fix and passes after; skills/sf-crawl/SKILL.md is back at its 50-line budget with no contract clause dropped.
evidence: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_crawl.py -v (21 tests OK, incl. test_unreadable_directory_reported_repo_relative; the test fails pre-fix with the absolute /private/var path in not_determined)

manual crawl of a $TMPDIR repo with a chmod-000 subdirectory: exit 0, not_determined carries 'could not read: restricted (counted only)', grep for the tmp root and $HOME across the artifact and JSON returns nothing
uvx --from ruff==0.17.0 ruff check . && python3 scripts/validate.py && python3 scripts/scan_public.py (all clean)
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (294 tests, 0 failures after CODEBASE.md regeneration)
